title: OSHA general industry materials handling and storage practice questions
description: Free OSHA materials handling practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart N: storage, rim wheels, cranes, crane inspections and slings, each linked to its source.

questions.question: Where mechanical handling equipment is used, what does 1910.176(a) require for aisles, loading docks, doorways and places where turns or passage must be made?

options.A: A guardrail along both sides of every aisle
options.C: A posted speed limit for each aisle
options.D: A spotter stationed at every turn

questions.explanation: 1910.176(a) states that where mechanical handling equipment is used, "sufficient safe clearances shall be allowed for aisles, at loading docks, through doorways and wherever turns or passage must be made."
questions.evidence: Where mechanical handling equipment is used, sufficient safe clearances shall be allowed for aisles, at loading docks, through doorways and wherever turns or passage must be made.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.176, Handling materials—general (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A rolling railroad car on a spur track could enter a building or a work area. What does 1910.176(f) require on that spur track?

options.A: A flagger posted at the building door
options.B: Wheel chocks on each car only
options.C: A warning bell at the track switch
options.D: Derail and/or bumper blocks

questions.explanation: 1910.176(f) states that "Derail and/or bumper blocks shall be provided on spur railroad tracks where a rolling car could contact other cars being worked, enter a building, work or traffic area."
questions.evidence: Derail and/or bumper blocks shall be provided on spur railroad tracks where a rolling car could contact other cars being worked, enter a building, work or traffic area.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.176, Handling materials—general (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: 1910.177 covers rim wheels used on large vehicles such as trucks, buses and off-road machines. Which rim wheel servicing does its scope paragraph exclude?

options.C: Rim wheels used on off-road machines
options.D: Single piece rim wheels used on trailers

questions.explanation: The section applies to rim wheels "used on large vehicles such as trucks, tractors, trailers, buses and off-road machines" and "does not apply to the servicing of rim wheels used on automobiles."
questions.evidence: This section applies to the servicing of multi-piece and single piece rim wheels used on large vehicles such as trucks, tractors, trailers, buses and off-road machines. It does not apply to the servicing of rim wheels used on automobiles,

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A restraining device or barrier must withstand the maximum force transferred to it during a rim wheel separation at what pressure, under 1910.177(d)(3)(i)?

options.A: 100 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.B: 110 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.C: 150 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure
options.D: 125 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure

questions.explanation: Each restraining device or barrier must withstand the force of "a rim wheel separation occurring at 150 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure for the type of rim wheel being serviced."
questions.evidence: Each restraining device or barrier shall have the capacity to withstand the maximum force that would be transferred to it during a rim wheel separation occurring at 150 percent of the maximum tire specification pressure for the type of rim wheel being serviced.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1910.177(d)(3)(iii) require restraining devices and barriers to be visually inspected?

options.A: Prior to each day's use and after any separation or sudden release of contained air
options.B: Once a week and after any separation of the rim wheel components
options.C: Once a month, with a written record
options.D: Only after a rim wheel separation has occurred

questions.explanation: Restraining devices and barriers "shall be visually inspected prior to each day's use and after any separation of the rim wheel components or sudden release of contained air."
questions.evidence: Restraining devices and barriers shall be visually inspected prior to each day's use and after any separation of the rim wheel components or sudden release of contained air.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.177, Servicing multi-piece and single piece rim wheels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In the multi-piece rim wheel procedure, a tire must be completely deflated before the rim wheel is removed from the axle when it has been driven underinflated at what level of its recommended pressure?

options.C: 60% or less
options.D: 70% or less

questions.explanation: 1910.177(f)(2) requires complete deflation by removing the valve core before removal from the axle "When the tire has been driven underinflated at 80% or less of its recommended pressure," or when there is obvious or suspected damage.

questions.question: Where must the rated load of an overhead or gantry crane be marked under 1910.179(b)(5)?

options.A: Only in the operator's manual kept in the office
options.B: On the runway rail next to the end stop
options.C: On a sign at the building entrance
options.D: Plainly on each side of the crane

questions.explanation: 1910.179(b)(5) states that "The rated load of the crane shall be plainly marked on each side of the crane." Each hoist of a crane with more than one hoisting unit is also marked, legible from the ground or floor.
questions.evidence: The rated load of the crane shall be plainly marked on each side of the crane,

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who does 1910.179(b)(8) permit to operate an overhead or gantry crane covered by the section?

options.A: Any employee who is 18 or older
options.B: Any employee who has watched a lift being made
options.C: Only designated personnel
options.D: Any employee who holds a driver's license

questions.explanation: 1910.179(b)(8) states: "Only designated personnel shall be permitted to operate a crane covered by this section."
questions.evidence: Only designated personnel shall be permitted to operate a crane covered by this section.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When lowering a load with an overhead or gantry crane, what is the fewest full wraps of rope 1910.179(n)(3)(viii) allows to remain on the hoisting drum?

options.C: None, if the hook reaches the floor
options.D: Two

questions.explanation: 1910.179(n)(3)(viii) states that "The load shall not be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum."
questions.evidence: The load shall not be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.179(j)(1)(ii) define the interval for periodic inspection of overhead and gantry cranes in regular service?

options.C: Every 2 to 5 years
options.D: Once every 3 years

questions.explanation: The rule designates two classifications: "Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals" and "Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals."
questions.evidence: (b) Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For the rated load test of an overhead or gantry crane, what upper limit does 1910.179(k)(2) set for test loads, unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise?

options.C: 125 percent of the rated load
options.D: 200 percent of the rated load

questions.explanation: 1910.179(k)(2) states: "Test loads shall not be more than 125 percent of the rated load unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer."
questions.evidence: Test loads shall not be more than 125 percent of the rated load unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the longest interval 1910.179(m)(1) allows between thorough inspections of all running ropes on an overhead or gantry crane?

options.C: Six months
options.D: Twelve months

questions.explanation: 1910.179(m)(1) states that "A thorough inspection of all ropes shall be made at least once a month," with a certification record kept on file.
questions.evidence: A thorough inspection of all ropes shall be made at least once a month

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.179, Overhead and gantry cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For crawler, locomotive and truck cranes, what upper limit does 1910.180(e)(2)(ii) set for rated load test loads?

options.A: 125 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.B: 150 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.C: 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius
options.D: 200 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius

questions.explanation: 1910.180(e)(2)(ii) states: "Test loads shall not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius."
questions.evidence: Test loads shall not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.180, Crawler locomotive and truck cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where does 1910.180(c)(2) require the load rating chart of a crawler, locomotive or truck crane to be fixed?

options.A: To the crane cab, easily visible to the operator while seated at the control station
options.B: In the employer's main office files
options.C: On a board at the entrance to the work area
options.D: Inside the toolbox stored on the crane

questions.explanation: The rating chart must be "securely fixed to the crane cab in a location easily visible to the operator while seated at his control station."
questions.evidence: A substantial and durable rating chart with clearly legible letters and figures shall be provided with each crane and securely fixed to the crane cab in a location easily visible to the operator while seated at his control station.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.180, Crawler locomotive and truck cranes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Each day before a sling is used, who does 1910.184(d) say must inspect the sling and all fastenings and attachments for damage or defects?

options.C: A Registered Professional Engineer
options.D: A competent person designated by the employer

questions.explanation: 1910.184(d) states: "Each day before being used, the sling and all fastenings and attachments shall be inspected for damage or defects by a competent person designated by the employer."
questions.evidence: Each day before being used, the sling and all fastenings and attachments shall be inspected for damage or defects by a competent person designated by the employer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.184(c)(14) state about slings without affixed and legible identification markings?

options.A: They may be used at half their rated capacity
options.C: They may be used for up to 30 days
options.D: They may be used if the operator approves

questions.explanation: 1910.184(c)(14) states: "Employers must not use slings without affixed and legible identification markings."
questions.evidence: Employers must not use slings without affixed and legible identification markings.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.184(c)(11) state about shock loading of slings?

options.B: It is allowed up to the sling's rated capacity
options.C: It is allowed with a basket hitch only
options.D: It is allowed once a competent person approves it

questions.explanation: Among the safe operating practices that apply whenever any sling is used, 1910.184(c)(11) states: "Shock loading is prohibited."
questions.evidence: Shock loading is prohibited.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A wire rope sling has randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay. At what count does 1910.184(f)(5)(i) require immediate removal from service?

options.C: Ten
options.D: Twenty-five

questions.explanation: Wire rope slings must be immediately removed from service for "Ten randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay, or five broken wires in one strand in one rope lay."
questions.evidence: Ten randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay, or five broken wires in one strand in one rope lay.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Above what temperature does 1910.184(e)(6) require an alloy steel chain sling that was heated to be permanently removed from service?

options.C: 2000 degrees F
options.D: 1000 degrees F

questions.explanation: 1910.184(e)(6) states that employers "must permanently remove an alloy steel-chain slings from service if it is heated above 1000 degrees F."
questions.evidence: Employers must permanently remove an alloy steel-chain slings from service if it is heated above 1000 degrees F.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.184(i)(6)(i), nylon web slings must not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of which substances are present?

options.C: Water or steam
options.D: Oils or greases

questions.explanation: 1910.184(i)(6)(i) states: "Nylon web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present." The caustics limit in (i)(6)(ii) is for polyester and polypropylene web slings.
questions.evidence: Nylon web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.184, Slings (as of Nov 3, 2026)
